name: Multi-Index Monte Carlo: the MIMC complexity theorem (Giles 2015, Theorem 2)

milestones.title: §2.4 — the telescoping sum of cross-differences
milestones.description: With $\Delta_d P_{\boldsymbol\ell}\equiv P_{\boldsymbol\ell}-P_{\boldsymbol\ell-\mathbf e_d}$ and the cross-difference $\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}\equiv\big(\prod_{d=1}^D\Delta_d\big)P_{\boldsymbol\ell}$, the cross-differences telescope: $\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\le\mathbf k}\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}=P_{\mathbf k}$ for every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb N^D$, the finite form of $\mathbb{E}[P]=\sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\ge\mathbf 0}\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol\Delta P_{\boldsymbol\ell}]$ (Giles 2015, §2.4, p. 13).

milestones.title: Theorem 2 — the case $\alpha_d \ge \tfrac12\beta_d$
milestones.description: Theorem 2 under the weaker condition $\alpha_d\ge\tfrac12\beta_d$ (equality allowed), where \"the form of the exponents is more complicated\" and the paper states none: the same three regimes with some exponents $e_1,e_2$ (Giles 2015, §2.4, Theorem 2, p. 14). The linked formal version has $e_1=2D_2+D$ and $e_2=(D_2-1)(2+\eta)+D$.
